court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Mrs.Sangeeta Chandresh Khandar vs Mrs.Chandresh Nanalal Khandar
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The parties are the Appellant-Mrs. Sangeeta Chandresh Khandar and Respondent-Mr. Chandresh Nanalal Khandar. They were married in 2009, but have been residing separately since October 20, 2008. The Respondent filed a petition for divorce under Section 13(1)(ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 against the Appellant. The parties have entered into Consent Terms.

legal_principles.principle: A party's consent to a divorce by mutual consent can be inferred from their actions and agreements.
legal_principles.held: The parties have been residing separately since 20.10.2008, which is a clear indication of their intention to dissolve the marriage.

legal_principles.principle: A party's undertaking to transfer property can be enforced through a court order.
legal_principles.held: The Respondent agrees and undertakes to transfer his rights, title and interests in the said residential flat... within 8 (Eight) weeks from the date of signing of the Consent Terms herein.

legal_principles.principle: A party's undertaking to repay a loan can be enforced through a court order.
legal_principles.held: The Respondent agrees and undertakes to fully repay the Bank Loan pertaining to the said residential flat, prior to transferring the same in the name of Appellant.

outcome.final_order: The Marriage Petition No. 12 of 2009 filed by the Respondent is converted into a petition filed under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 seeking divorce by mutual consent.
